title: stage masks: resolution
shortDescription: Séance Photographs: one drifting ectoplasm fog masks three framed spirit photographs, its mask targets at scale 1, 0.5 and 0.25 side by side, with the bytes of each — soft fog looks the same at a sixteenth of the memory, hard edges show the grid
description:
Three framed cabinet cards on the wall of a spirit photographer's back parlour: the same plate in each, a widow in mourning black in a carved chair. Where the ectoplasm drifts over a photograph, it shows the plate as the medium sold it — the studio gone cold, a veiled figure standing behind her chair with its long hands on her shoulders, ectoplasm streaming from her lips.

A `StageDirector` with four slots: the parlour with the living plates at the bottom, and above it one slot per frame with the spirit plate of that frame, masked by a living fog. The three masks differ only in `StageMaskOptions.scale` — `new StageMask(fogStage, {scale})` — so the director draws each fog stage into a pass target of that share of the drawing buffer and samples it up with the texture's filtering. **Three fog stages, not one**: a pass target belongs to its stage, so one stage has one scale, and two masks on one stage that ask for different scales are refused. The three stages draw the same fog from one clock that the page writes once per frame, so only the resolution of their targets tells them apart.

The plaque under each frame shows the size of its mask target at the current canvas size and pixel ratio — the logical size × the pixel ratio × the scale, rounded down — and its bytes: the colour in the renderer's output buffer type (8 B per pixel for RGBA half-float) plus the depth buffer every pass target carries (4 B per pixel). The panel adds the same at 3840 × 2160: about 100 MB at scale 1, 25 MB at 0.5, 6 MB at 0.25. *mask edges* (key E) switches the fog between soft blobs and hard-edged ectoplasm with thin trailing threads: the soft fog looks the same at every scale, while the hard edge steps and blurs on the coarser grid and the threads, thinner than a texel, break up and fall through it. *scales* sets all three at once, or each panel on its own; a new scale is a new `StageMask` — the options are read once — and the old one comes off its slot before the new one goes on. *fog drifts* (space) holds the clock. See [Stage masks: a mask at a share of the resolution](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#a-mask-at-a-share-of-the-resolution) and [what a mask costs](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#what-a-mask-costs).
